doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: First pro gig in Newport, Kentucky with Eddie Cleanhead Vinson
summary: His mother reluctantly sends him across the river, and he plays with Eddie Cleanhead Vinson, whom he calls a consummate jazz player and the composer of Tune Up and Four.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: my mother Bec, her name was Rebecca. “Bec, the bass player didn’t show up, can you sent Michael over?” to what was Newport, Kentucky, which was the Las Vegas, Sin City of the world. Everything went on over there. And you know what my mother said to him? “Are you out of your mind? Send my baby over there with those cut-throats?” Silence on the phone. But she had to back off. Because the year before that I turned professional doo-wopper and she said I couldn’t go. And she found my clothes in the hallway and she found out that I was going anyway so she gave me what little money she had and sent me on my way. So she saw this is who my son is. If I tell him no he’s going to go anyway. So finally she says okay and put me in a taxi and sent me over there. And I began to play with Eddie “Cleanhead” Vincent.
Oh no kidding? Wow. So you were playing a mix of jazz and blues?
He was a consummate jazz player. He wrote “Tune Up.”

He wrote “Four” — Miles Davis stole them. But I knew that then see so I’m not just coming in this music like — I’m not going to mention any music schools but it’s a little more like destiny like. Like you need to know, to get this stuff. And this is what’s good about this interview because not everybody took the path that I took. So go ahead.
